In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the n/p effective mass splitting is not yet a well established fact in the nuclear matter equation of state.
the n/p effective mass splitting is a relevant observable for HIC at intermediate energies.

a careful and accurate study of the n/p mass splittings in HIC at intermediate energies, with a proper selection of the emitted particle momenta, can be an important probe of the MD of the in-medium NN interaction in isovector channel.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the isospin MD of the nuclear mean-field is a key ingredient to be taken into account for a realistic description of the dynamics of asymmetric nuclear matter.
the MD of the n/p effective mass splitting in asymmetric nuclear matter is an important ingredient for transport simulations of heavy ion collisions.

, in order to get reliable results for the MD of the isospin effective nucleon–nuclear interaction in asymmetric matter, one has to consider the momentum dependence of the isovector NN interaction, the momentum dependence of n/p mass splitting and the momentum dependent isospin asymmetry of the system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MD in the n/p effective mass splitting is a very important ingredient in the description of HIC at intermediate energies.
a careful analysis of the n/p effective mass splitting is possible in HIC at intermediate energies, in spite of the limited charge asymmetry of such systems.

the MD of the isovector part of the effective nucleon-nucleon interaction in neutron-rich nuclear matter is expected to be a key ingredient in order to understand the isospin dependence of collective flows in HIC.
